body.x: ViewMagine (CEO Do-yeop Kim) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Established in 2020, ViewMagine uses vision technology and drones to provide construction quality control solutions. Within 3 years of its establishment, it was able to attract 2.1 billion KRW of investments, and is actively conducting business, succeeding in expanding not just to major construction companies in Korea, but to Japan as well.

ViewMagine’s ‘VODA’ is a platform to control and monitor the quality of architecture and is a solution to prevent the structure damage of assets. An official explained that it is capable of detecting cracks as small as 0.3mm in width and is more than twice as fast and capable of reducing costs by over 30%.

In the future, they are planning to release an online web platform that supplies detailed information of defects to construction managers, inspectors, and various stakeholders. The platform can be used to request analysis of building data obtained from drones and the analysis data will indicate the shape of the crack, type, size, date, and location on a 2D or 3D model.
In addition, they showcased ‘VM100’, a mobile drone station. It can charge drones, store them, transmit data in real-time, and can be applied to all types of drones.

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
